anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Its approved L1 baseline has a small but genuinely 3D, depth-sorted mine: visible voxel materials, camera rotation, frontmost-face ray clicks, and extraction hazards. The assigned chart is 2D and has no depth, physics, or hazard interaction, but it adds an unknown fleet and indirect band/block/count search. This makes the L1 anchor a lower-complexity spatial-control reference without treating the two different mechanics as strictly dominant in every dimension.

evidence.explanation: The approved baseline is L1/simplified and its active profiles expose voxel targets, sealing stones, lava, support, and durability parameters.

The UI rotates the mine and uses a frontmost raycast for canvas mining.
The grader independently replays click rays, material outcomes, durability, and extraction state.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 baseline is a continuously changing physics task with three ordered lamps, walls, wells, momentum, and a 500 ms observation window; its full surface is a continuously held analog drag. The assigned L2 chart has a zero observation window, no autonomous ticks, and state changes only after a designation is fired. The chart's dependent search is real planning, but it is materially below the live control and recovery burden of this L3 anchor.

evidence.explanation: The approved configuration uses three lamps/walls/wells, faster dynamics, continuous full control, and a 500 ms observation window.

The grader replays physics ticks and collision state before requiring the ordered lamps and cup.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 baseline requires a hidden die orientation to survive movement through five barriers and face gates, with sparse scanner reveals and a bounded roll route. The assigned chart exposes its block directions and has no movement, orientation algebra, barriers, or live state. Even its hardest profile remains a static constraint/search problem, so L2 is below this L4 reference.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 baseline requires four changing-board swaps, exact score, cascades, gravity/refill effects, and a shrinking visible refill preview. The assigned environment's shots change the evidence set and fleet candidates, but the chart geometry and target world do not mutate and there are no cascades or inventory transformations. The assigned L5 profile is therefore below this approved L5 task in state-changing planning burden; its label is a named profile, not evidence that it matches the anchor's empirical difficulty.

visible_baseline_solution: From the initial screenshot, read the visible band numbers, each bracket's A/B/C block label and arrow direction, the vessel-length manifest, the no-touch rule, the orientation-feedback rule, and the two available sweeps. In Full mode, drag the Band, Block, and Count rotary selectors to their labeled detents and click FIRE. Use a star only when a whole run is worth a sweep charge; otherwise fire an exact visible count. After every shot, keep the persistent miss, hit, orientation, and sunk marks in the current screenshot and update the possible straight vessel placements using the known lengths and no-touch rule. Avoid invalid or repeated designations and continue until the manifest reads all vessels sunk, then certify. The chart is static between actions: the configured observation window is zero and one frame is returned, so a recent frame sequence is not needed. Completion is the pass condition; fewer shots only improves the efficiency score.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current L2/full assignment is source-supported. Relative to the d1 profile it adds a fifth-by-eighth irregular chart, randomized block boundaries and labels, and a third hidden vessel; relative to d3 it does not require local reversal of count direction; relative to d4 it retains non-touching vessels and orientation feedback. The full rotary surface adds spatial control precision but leaves the L2 world and search problem intact. It is below the approved live-physics L3, hidden-orientation L4, and changing-board L5 anchors, while being more than the approved L1 mine's direct exposed-target extraction in indirect search burden.

findings.affected_configurations: Difficulty 3, both Simplified and Full, for seeds whose generated runs all have reverse=false
findings.claim: The d2-to-d3 distinction is not guaranteed per generated instance.
findings.causal_explanation: When reverse_counts is enabled, the generator independently samples one Boolean for each run. It does not require any sampled run to be reversed. If every run is false, d3 has the same dimensions, block layout, count direction, orientation feedback, touching rule, holes, fleet lengths, and sweeps as d2; the effective screenshot task then differs only in hidden condition/task identity. Source proves the collapse is possible, but not its observed frequency or whether a particular multi-seed sample hits it.

evidence.explanation: d2 and d3 differ in their declared world parameters only by reverse_counts.
Each run uses rng.randrange(2) under reverse_counts, with no at-least-one-reversed assertion; that same Boolean controls count values.
The intended screenshot-visible distinction is the run arrow, which disappears when all sampled reverse flags are false.

findings.recommended_action: Make the d3 generator guarantee at least one reversed run, or otherwise regenerate/reject an all-forward d3 instance before exposing it as level 3. Parent multi-seed checks should quantify the current frequency.

findings.affected_configurations: All five difficulty levels and both interaction modes in the browser runtime
findings.claim: The exact fleet placement is shipped in public browser state and consumed by the UI.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator places a copy of the fleet in public_state.runtime_fleet. The browser builds its target map from that field and computes hit, orientation, and sunk marks from it. A compliant screenshot-only solver cannot inspect page state because the task forbids it, so this does not make the visible baseline easier under the stated protocol; it does create a page-state bypass and weakens the separation between public UI state and hidden truth if that boundary is not enforced externally.

evidence.explanation: The task explicitly requires screenshots/visible controls and forbids DOM, page-state, and hidden-state inspection.
public_state includes runtime_fleet while truth separately includes fleet.

The grader requires public runtime_fleet to equal truth, confirming that the field is part of the submitted public contract.

findings.recommended_action: If the local evaluation boundary is intended to protect hidden placement, keep fleet coordinates out of public_state and provide hit/sunk feedback through an authoritative action path; retain the explicit visible-only policy for agents.

findings.affected_configurations: All five difficulty levels and both interaction modes
findings.claim: The task's ‘as few shots as possible’ wording is an optimization score, not a success requirement.
findings.causal_explanation: The natural-language task asks for as few shots as possible, but the grader passes whenever all vessels are sunk and calculates efficiency afterward from the omniscient minimum divided by shots. There is no shot budget or minimum-efficiency threshold for pass/fail. Thus the search-quality objective is optional for completion, even though it remains visible in the score/readout.

evidence.explanation: The task wording explicitly requests sinking every vessel with as few shots as possible.
Pass is based on all vessels sunk; efficiency is returned as a separate score after completion.
The UI displays shot count and says fewer shots earn a higher score, but does not make it a completion gate.

findings.recommended_action: Clarify in the task specification that shot count is scored rather than required for pass, or make the intended efficiency threshold authoritative if search quality is part of success.

concise_summary: Keep the current Coordinates by Another Name L2/full baseline: its irregular 2D indirect-addressing search is above the L1 mine reference and below the approved live-physics, hidden-orientation, and changing-board anchors. The five named profiles form an otherwise upward ladder, but d3 must guarantee a reversed run to distinguish it from d2 on every generated instance. Separate source-proven public fleet exposure and the score-versus-pass wording are additional boundary/specification findings.
limitations: No browser, runtime generation, multi-seed, grader, or exported-verifier checks were performed; the parent is responsible for those checks.
No human or computer-use-agent calibration evidence was available in the supplied source.
No historical pre-controls implementation was supplied, so historical fixed-seed preservation remains unknown.
